chapter: Postwar records, Miami and Los Angeles
title: Tito Puente as a young musician
summary: Machito praises Puente as talented, always on time, ambitious and dedicated, already known to Curbelo.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: What the word "jazz" means: origins, Dixieland and labels

blocks.x: Is Tito Puente in any of those live Decca's recordings that you made from La Conga?
Yes
He is.
'Nague' ....
Well, I know he recorded 'Nague' with you in 1942, but he is also at La Conga on the live one recordings?
Yes
Okay, what kind of musician was Tito Puente at that time?
Very good. He always was talented.
Okay, do you have any other observations about Tito? Was he dependable? Did he show up on time?
Definetely. Always on time, always. He was possibly, one of the most responsible persons that I ever met in my life.
Okay, at that time did he show any future promise of being the great musician he is today?
Yes, always.
Was he into arranging and learning music and that?

Uh - Huh. He was, as a matter of fact, he is one of the most dedicated persons that I ever met. A young fellow, because he was very young, he was about seventeen years old, so when I met him he was about fourteen and he was good already.
Did he have any girlfriends at the time?
Well, he was going out with his, actually, his wife, the mother of his first child, and she came from a very nice family. They was a very nice couple.
Did Puente seemed serious to you while he was in the band, like, you know, this is my life, I am going to, I am going to try to be the best some day? Did he give you that impression?

He was always ambitious and his ambition was - it wasn't to - I mean, to interfere anybody, he just, he was in love with what he was doing; and he was paying attention to every little thing that you don't realize that he was paying attention.
Okay, did he already know Jose Curbelo?
Yes.
